ecosystem.notes: Alphabet reports no gross flow volume for its platforms, so measure is null. payouts is TAC: FY2025 TAC was $59.926B. The 10-K defines it as amounts paid to distribution partners (browser providers, mobile carriers, OEMs, software developers) and to Google Network partners. The 10-K says the TAC rate (TAC as a percentage of advertising revenues) decreased from 20.7% to 20.3% from 2024 to 2025. platformRevenue is Google advertising revenues ($294.69B) because TAC is measured against advertising. Total Alphabet revenues were $402.836B. YouTube creator payments are not in TAC. The 10-K puts them inside 'content acquisition costs' in other cost of revenues and gives no separate amount. The YouTube $100B study figure is company-reported, covers four years in total (Jan 2021–Dec 2024) and is not an FY2025 flow; it is kept because no newer edition was looked up in this refresh. Its source URL is on services.google.com, Google's own file host; the records validator's search-page check (/google\./) would wrongly flag it.

economicActivity.label: Economic activity Google helped provide
economicActivity.definition: Google's own estimate of the economic activity that Google Search, Google Ads, Google Cloud, AdSense/AdMob, Ad Grants, YouTube and Google Play helped provide for a state's businesses, nonprofits, publishers, creators and developers. Modeled by the Google Economics team (e.g. $8 of profit per $1 of Google Ads spend), not measured output, not GDP and not Google's own spending. States reported in millions are converted to billions (shown in square brackets in the quote).

businesses.label: Businesses using Google's free tools
businesses.definition: Businesses in the state that "used Google's tools at no cost to receive phone calls, bookings, reviews, requests for directions, or other direct connections to their customers". Always reported as "more than".

investment.label: Cumulative Google investment in the state
investment.period: cumulative, from the year the state's first data center was built through the 2025 report
investment.definition: Google's statement that it "has invested more than" (Georgia: "has committed more than ... of investment") the amount in the state since its data center(s) there were built. The 2025 report says "Investment methodology now reflects total data center investment (construction, server and networking infrastructure)", so these figures are on a broader basis than the 2024 edition's and are not comparable with it. Reported only for the 13 states with Google data centers; cumulative, not annual.

longLivedAssets.label: Long-lived assets
longLivedAssets.definition: Property and equipment, net, plus operating lease assets, by geographic area (10-K Note 15). Columns are 2024 then 2025; the 2025 value is recorded.

footprint.notes: Source: Google's own 2025 U.S. Economic Impact Report (national PDF with one page per state, data for calendar 2025, PDF created April 2026), the newest edition (economicimpact.google, checked 2026-11-24); it replaces the 2024 edition. The methodology page credits the Google Economics team and its own multipliers (Hal Varian's $2 profit per $1 ad spend, a 70% organic-click adjustment, giving $8 of profit per $1 of Google Ads spend), with no outside author named, so tier is company-published, not commissioned; the economic-activity figures are model estimates of value to other businesses, not Google spending. 50 states + DC have economic activity and business counts; Puerto Rico has a page too ($330 million, 154,000+ businesses) but is not a state, so it is left out. Nebraska's body text reads "more than $4.2 of economic activity" (the word billion is missing), so its quote includes the page's headline "$4.2+ billion of economic activity". Investment figures exist only for the 13 states with data centers and are cumulative since each data center was built; the 2025 report says its investment methodology "now reflects total data center investment (construction, server and networking infrastructure)", so the figures are much higher than the 2024 edition's (Iowa $20 billion vs $6.8 billion) and the two editions are not comparable. The report also gives philanthropic giving, volunteer hours and Ad Grants by state; not recorded. Google publishes no employees-by-state figures here (nationally: more than 100,000 U.S. full-time employees at the end of 2025, offices and data centers in 26 states). The FY2025 10-K gives no property breakdown by state or country, so sites are the HQ (10-K Item 2) plus 11 data centers as described on the 2025 state pages. No employee, office or tax breakdown by country was found; the only geographic split of physical footprint in the 10-K is long-lived assets (property and equipment plus operating lease assets), United States $195,337 million vs International $66,481 million at Dec 31, 2025, recorded as one country row and one region row (the 2024 comparatives in the same table match the values previously stored).
